meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Swiss Confederation; legal seat to be designated in a specified Swiss canton, commonly Zug, Geneva, or Zurich)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic system based on the Swiss Federal Code of Obligations and cantonal administrative law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1 November 1986, in force 1 March 1987)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 25 January 2013, in force 1 January 2014)
EFTA-China Free Trade Agreement (signed 25 November 2013, in force 1 July 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0, as amended, notably arts. 3-8, 9 and 22; Federal Act on the Implementation of the Recommendations of the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes of 28 September 2012, SR 267.0; Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220, arts. 620 et seq., 697k et seq. (UBO and bearer-share transparency registers), 716b and 922 et seq.; Swiss Criminal Code, SR 311.0, arts. 305bis and 305ter; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) of 17 October 2007, SR 221.411.1; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA), SR 955.011.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or government-issued identification of each founding shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document's country of origin, confirmed by the competent Apostille authority or consular office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Switzerland, China, and all other contracting states; Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current extract from the commercial register and certificate of good standing of any corporate founder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership certificate and UBO register extract of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, company secretary, or statutory auditor of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Swiss formation agent, notary, or fiduciary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's jurisdiction, with Swiss notarial acknowledgment where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all founders, directors, officers, and 25%-plus beneficial owners, comprising automated and manual screening against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Swiss SECO sanctions list (SR 946.231.11), and recognised international PEP databases; adverse-media and global-watchlist checks are required. Screening results, rationales, and risk ratings must be recorded in the client due diligence file and retained for at least ten years under AMLA standards; for low-risk EdTech subscription business, Level-1 standard customer due diligence applies unless a PEP, sanctions hit, or anomalous ownership structure elevates the file to enhanced due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch) plus the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) for the intended Swiss canton
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory firm name must be truthful, distinct, and non-deceptive under art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and HRegV requirements. The name may be formed in an official Swiss language or in a recognised foreign-language form, but non-Latin script names are registered in Roman transliteration; a secondary auxiliary name in Chinese or other script may appear in brackets only if it does not mislead or conflict with the registered legal form. The legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'Société anonyme', 'Società anonima', or the accepted abbreviations 'AG' / 'SA' must be present in the firm name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed firm name, the applicant may require the Cantonal Commercial Register Office to issue a formal written decision (Verfügung). The applicant may submit an administrative objection to the cantonal commercial register authority within thirty days of receipt, and further appeal the decision to the competent Cantonal Administrative Court. A final limited appeal lies with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. The applicant may also file a fresh name-clearance request after removing the conflicting element or obtaining the required regulatory consent; name availability is re-tested as of the new filing date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft must maintain a genuine registered office at a physical address within a Swiss commune. A virtual office or professional domiciliation service at a Swiss fiduciary, attorney, or business centre is accepted where the address is a real physical office, company books and documents are accessible, and an authorised person can accept service of process. A pure letterbox or PO Box arrangement is inadmissible and may lead to refusal of registration or subsequent removal from the commercial register. For the EdTech language-learning subscription business, professional domiciliation at a reputable Swiss service provider is accepted on a low-risk basis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: below 10% for a clean low-risk EdTech subscription company using a professional domiciliation address; approximately 15-25% if the registered office is a mass virtual-office business centre with large numbers of co-registered companies, or if an ultimate beneficial owner is a PEP, appears on a sanctions list, or generates an AMLA suspicious-activity report. Unannounced on-site inspections are rare in the absence of AML/CTF flags but may be conducted by commercial register authorities, tax authorities, prosecutors, or the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS) under statutory investigation powers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC) publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and SOGC publisher

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service at a Swiss fiduciary or business centre (first twelve months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CHF 1,500-4,000 per year depending on canton, service scope, and risk profile

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal, physical minute book, share certificates, and filing of initial UBO and shareholders registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark charge for standard preparation set

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Articles 620-731 (Aktiengesellschaft / Stock Company formation and governance), and the Swiss Merger Act (FusG) as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) with official Federal Registry interface at zefix.ch.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Formation (Gründungsurkunde / Acte constitutif) together with the Commercial Register Declaration (Anmeldung / Déclaration) in the officially recognized cantonal form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up prior to registration, with payment evidenced by an escrow/blocked capital certificate in a Swiss bank within the cantonal registry's accepted list. Shareholder loans or contribution in kind are not permitted to satisfy the paid-up minimum without an audited asset valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned founding shareholders, hereby resolve in writing: 1. The entire subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000 has been lawfully allocated and the paid-up portion of CHF 50,000 is held in a blocked escrow account established for incorporation purposes. 2. The registered office of the company is fixed at [Place], Switzerland. 3. The board of directors is constituted, and the following officers are appointed with sole or collegial signature rights: Chairperson [Name], CEO [Name], and Finance & Compliance Delegate [Name]. 4. Each officer accepts the appointment and confirms compliance with the statutory diligence duty. 5. The board is authorized to execute all notarized forms, submit the commercial register application, and obtain the VAT number and any required municipal permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize Articles of Association and Obtain Notarized Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat / Étude notariale) authorized by the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and settle the articles of association (Statuten / Statuts) containing the corporate name, purpose (incl. educational technology and language-learning software), registered office, share capital, share classes, board structure, and audit provision. Arrange a physical notarization appointment; all founding shareholders must appear in person or by irrevocable authorization. The notary will jointly certify incorporation in one public deed and the declaration by the board members. The notary files the required certificate of de-escalation of tax obligations with the cantonal tax authority where applicable.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or company extract for each founding shareholder
Audited Swiss bank certificate confirming paid-up minimum capital in a blocked escrow account
Drafted Articles of Association
List of board members with addresses and nationality
Consents of board members to serve
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the capital certificate or the permitted purpose, cure by either obtaining a corrected bank certificate or amending the articles within 10 business days and re-notarizing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Deposit Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss Bank or branch with a domicile in Switzerland; standard major banks include UBS, Credit Suisse (now part of UBS), and cantonal banks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an escrow deposit account in the new company's name, expressly designated for incorporation capital. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 (one-half of the statutory minimum of CHF 100,000) from shareholder funds. Obtain an official blocked-capital certificate (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung / Attestation de blocage) confirming that funds remain dedicated to incorporation and cannot be released until the commercial register has registered the company.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Incorporation application or notary letters
Identification of beneficial owners and economic purpose for AML profiling
Board resolutions appointing the bank contact
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires an enhanced economic substance questionnaire due to the online EdTech subscription model, deliver the business plan, target market, and AML risk rating; escalate to the bank's commercial client onboarding desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application to the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) in the canton of the registered office; electronic filing via Zefix portal or direct courier.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized public deed, the annual financial statement waiver for the first period (if applicable), the paid-up capital certificate, and the complete shareholders'/board member identification. The registry verifies the company name against trademark databases and legal form. Upon approval, the registry publishes an entry in the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB). After registration, obtain the confirmed Extract (Handelsregisterauszug / Extrait du registre du commerce).
required_dossiers: Notarized Public Deed of Formation
Blocked-capital bank certificate
Shareholder identification and proof of signature
Consent to board and auditor (if any)
Domiciliation agreement for registered office
Power of attorney for filing (if not notarized)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal deficiency letter (e.g., missing financial annual report waiver), cure within the statutory deadline by submitting the signed waiver or amended notarial deed; if the name is rejected, file a new name election through the fee-based preliminary name check and resubmit within the responding period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for VAT and Obtain Federal Statistical/Tax Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFFD), VAT Division, and directly after commercial registry registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the commercial registry registration is effective, the company is automatically registered for direct federal tax and cantonal/communal tax. For VAT, if worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 annually, submit the mandatory VAT registration form (Form 05) via e-services or in writing. For intra-Community transactions and digital subscription platforms, register for the OSS if serving EU customers, although not required for the founding deed. Keep records of corporate bank account and Swift/BIC for future tax payments.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Articles of Association
Form 05 for Swiss VAT registration
Proof of board identity and signature
Billing address certificate or domiciliation letter (if using Geneva or Zug provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT office demands evidence of effective head office or digital economic presence, provide a lease agreement for the registered office and board member employment records; a change of fictional domicile may trigger reclassification, therefore cure by maintaining economic substance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canton of registered office: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs / Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit (AWA) - only for non-industrial premises; no special industrial manufacturing permit exists for pure software EdTech subscription services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - online software activity falls under the free federal guarantee of trade under Art. 31 of the Federal Constitution and the Code of Obligations; no industrial operating permit is required unless physical office use exceeds regulatory thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) / Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Voluntary exemption: the software development, server hosting, and online tutoring activity do not fall within Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (EIAO) since there is no physical production plant, warehouse, or extraction activity; the general duty to emit environmental harm under Art. 2 EPA is nevertheless observed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office use, local municipal wastewater ordinance (kommunale Gewässerschutzverordnung) and air quality thresholds per Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) apply. Cloud server emissions are assessed indirectly as embodied electricity consumption and must be reported in the QR code of the digital taxation statement; no facility discharge stream exists for pure software operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical office leased by the company: a fire safety clearance (Feuerpolizeiliche Abnahme) for use of business premises, structural load inspection for server racks/electrical panels above 100kg/m2, work safety and health directives of Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) are required before full operational scale; if employees work from home only, a written occupational safety stress-risk assessment is required per the Swiss Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (VUV/ArbG 3 et seq.).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA), Berne, Switzerland; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch, including the VAT, UID-Register and company tax e-Services portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must apply for a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) via the Swiss Federal Statistical Office UID register, then file Form 11 (application for VAT registration for non-established businesses) with the ESTV main VAT department using the official e-Service platform. The application requires certified company incorporation documents, proof of foreign registration, particulars of Swiss place of business or Swiss tax representative, description of activities, expected Swiss turnover, and bank details. VAT registration is mandatory if the annual worldwide turnover generated from taxable supplies in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000; voluntary registration is permitted for non-residents (Art. 11 and 14 MWSTG). The ESTV issues the UID and MWST-Nummer within approximately 5 to 10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Swiss federal corporate income tax (8.5% on profit after tax, equivalent to roughly 7.8% pre-tax) plus cantonal and communal profit taxes, giving standard all-in effective rates of approximately 11.9% to 15.0% depending on canton (e.g., Zug); taxation is blended territorial/worldwide for resident companies; global active business income is taxable with credit/participation relief, but passive foreign income is generally taxable. No pass-through treatment applies to the AG, and no US-style check-the-box classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Swiss law. Available statutory mechanisms include: group taxation / tax consolidation under Art. 59 para 5 DBG (federal) and matching cantonal rules, permitting intra-group profit and loss offset between Swiss resident group companies; VAT group registration (elected group treatment) for units closely linked by economic, organisational and financial relationships (Art. 21 MWSTG); small business VAT exemption election for turnover below CHF 100,000 (Art. 11 MWSTG); election to apply domestic reverse-charge or to zero-rate export services upon documented foreign place of use; election to withhold or op to be treated as an invoice-based taxpayer; hybrid mismatch adjustments under Art. 59a DBG are mandatory, not elective, and apply against foreign hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, MWST/TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover (exclusive of VAT) from taxable supplies performed in Switzerland (Art. 10, 11, 14 MWSTG); non-established suppliers of digital, telecommunication and e-commerce B2C services are taxable from the first franc of Swiss supplies if that CHF 100,000 threshold is reached; separate reduced registration threshold of CHF 50,000 applies only to businesses established in Switzerland deriving supplies of professional/institutional services to other VAT payers; no registration threshold applies to non-established businesses deriving supplies of services and goods located or used in Switzerland unless excluded by tax treaty rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland operates no real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction control, no unitel API, and no digital stamping of e-invoices. Swiss law mandates the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) for payment slips attached to invoices in CHF; the vendor may issue ordinary paper/PDF invoices if VAT data fields comply with Art. 26 MWSTG. E-bill (SIX eBill) and other EDI/e-invoicing formats (e.g., Peppol BIS, Faktur-X) are voluntary commercial standards. Mandatory fiscalisation is limited to cash register software meeting the Federal Department of Finance's technical safety requirements for retail transactions; cloud-based EdTech subscription billing is outside this regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% Swiss VAT is available for: (i) exported movable goods, including digital content stored on physical media; (ii) services that relate to movable property that will be exported; (iii) services supplied directly to non-resident customers and properly attributable to use or benefit outside Switzerland (including distance B2B and B2C digital learning subscriptions where the customer's residence and place of use is abroad); and (iv) services relating to immovable property located abroad. For EdTech subscriptions sold through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing to Swiss consumers, the non-established app store operator is deemed the supplier under Art. 20a MWSTG and must charge Swiss VAT; the Swiss AG cannot zero-rate those supplies. Zero-rating for the AG applies only where the customer is a non-established business or private user abroad supplied on an own-account basis without platform intermediation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss export declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration / GemData drop-off declaration or REX certificate for corresponding shipments)
Commercial invoice referencing 0% export rate, contract terms, and delivery conditions (Incoterms)
Transport document evidencing physical departure from Switzerland: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or postal/courier consignment note
Proof of receipt abroad: customs clearance confirmation of destination country, signed delivery note, or import declaration
For digital services: contractual documentation, IP address or geolocation evidence of the customer, unique customer identification, and confirmation of foreign establishment or residence
Payment documentation showing foreign-source settlement (e.g., SWIFT credits, remittance advices)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SFTA may retrospectively disallow zero-rating, reassess turnover at 8.1% standard rate, disallow related input VAT deductions, and claim interest of 5% per annum. Where evasion is established under Art. 69 MWSTG, the penalty is up to three times the evaded tax, with a maximum of CHF 250,000, and attempt or obstruction is punishable by fines up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 70 MWSTG. Missing, contradictory, or late-procured export documentation at the time of filing invalidates the zero-rating claim and exposes the AG to a reassessment up to 10 years after each VAT period. Intentional misapplication of export zero-rating, including the use of false residence certificates in B2C EdTech subscriptions, triggers criminal prosecution, publication of sanctions in the official gazette, and suspension from the VAT electrical network. Swiss law imposes no statutory foreign exchange repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark is used by the SFTA to test commercial bona fides; unrepatriated export proceeds with no payment evidence beyond 180 days are treated as indicia of fictitious exports and lead to immediate clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised capital and current account regime. The Swiss franc is freely convertible in spot and forward markets; neither import, export, nor capital-movement licences are required. Profit remittance, dividends, and loan interest may flow freely to non-residents, but the board must allocate legal reserves at 5% of paid-in capital and 20% of share capital before dividends. No exchange control clearance is needed for remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender obligations exist. Export receipts may be retained in any currency, converted at any time, and no repatriation deadline or minimum conversion ratio is imposed by the SNB or Swiss FX authorities. The only obligation is statistical reporting for Swiss balance of payments purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for offshore EMIs. Offshore digital e-money institutions — such as UK-licensed Wise or EU-licensed Revolut — may hold CHF via partner banks, but for a Swiss AG exercising capital escrow obligations they cannot replace a licensed Swiss bank. Legal constraints: FINMA prohibits accepting public deposits without a banking licence; an EMI's safeguarding arrangement does not constitute statutory depositor protection; and the tax authorities and commercial registry generally require an official Swiss confirmation of capital payment. For operating current accounts, an offshore EMI is viable, but regulatory subjection of the EdTech company only arises if the company itself forwards money; the company must not act as an agent for onboarding third-party customers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically. A Swiss-resident director may submit a notarised copy of passport and apostilled corporate documents; a video identification meeting with the bank's compliance officer is the current standard for low-risk AGs. Foreign-resident directors will typically need to attend in person at a Swiss branch or provide a recognised electronic identification certificate issued by a FINMA-compliant provider. The AG's economic substance, actual office location and board residence profile influence the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital paid up by a foreign parent after incorporation delays exceeding statutory time limit or paid below 100% nominal value
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement or confirmation from the prior escrow account, board resolution on capital pay-up, Swiss bank payment order copy, audited disclosure under the Commercial Register, and notarised declarations of all UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Swiss or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date shareholders register, register report from the Commercial Register, UBO declaration sworn by the board, organisational chart of the parent group, and audited financial statements if an intermediate holding vehicle is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound digital subscription micropayments from Apple/Google platforms creating aggregation of unverified third-party payers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding platform agreements with Apple and Google, merchant account statements, transaction log aggregation method, privacy policy audit, and contractual warranties that all underlying users are end consumers not subject to Swiss anti-money laundering monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border IP licensing with a low-tax Swiss interposed company until the EdTech AG's substance is proven
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP ownership certificates, technical activity roadmap, employment listings, software maintenance logs, board minutes approving licensing terms, transfer pricing documentation under the Swiss circular, and tax clearance for the transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: send a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder to the Swiss bank's IBAN designated for the capital escrow. Include Remittance Information 'AG 30.1 Share capital — [amount] CHF' and ISO 20022 Purpose Code 'EQUI' or 'CFIN'. The bank must submit an SNB statistical report under the Balance of Payments Ordinance; the account is freed only after confirmation of sworn statement under Art. 652g CO. Verification: sign board resolution and submit a capital repayment form with certified signatures; provide the external notary with the statutory vesting confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier payments, licensing royalties, and SaaS infrastructure costs; MT202 for banc-to-banc clearing if the beneficiary is not directly on the same payment system. For high-value hardware procurement, a clean or documentary letter of credit may be issued under UCP 600, with SWIFT MT700/760 confirmation. Recurring low-value payments may be settled via SEPA EUR and SIC/CH-IN CHF clearing. Every outward payment needs a purpose code per SNB reporting, no foreign exchange permission is needed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright spot and outright forward contracts with a Swiss licensed bank (free of FINMA licensing because the contract is the user's treasury operation)
FX swaps executed under ISDA/CSA with a counterparty bank (allowed as an OTC derivative subject to margin under EMIR only if the principal exceeds CHF 8 billion; typical EdTech is below threshold)
Currency options (OTC) on CHF/EUR/USD written by regulated banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic non-CHF currencies if the underlying exposure is an illiquid market rate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Federal and Cantonal combined)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (on behalf of the Swiss Confederation and the canton)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the usual deadline is 31 May / 30 June of the following year, with extension normally obtainable upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid tax, administrative fines under cantonal tax statutes, and criminal prosecution for deliberate concealment or false returns; no direct administrative strike-off effect.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, board report, and statutory audit report (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; submitted to the tax authority as part of the corporate tax return; not filed publicly with the Commercial Register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Balance sheet date plus six months for AGM approval of the annual accounts pursuant to Art. 699 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; submission with tax return by the applicable tax filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of directors, court-ordered statutory review, and administrative penalties for failure to keep proper books; persistent non-compliance can ultimately lead to compulsory winding-up or strike-off by the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return or VAT final settlement declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of each assigned VAT accounting period (quarterly or annually as determined by ESTV); annual filers submit the annual return after the business year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest, administrative fine of up to CHF 800 for late filing, and penal orders up to CHF 8,000 for VAT evasion; no commercial-register strike-off consequence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner register confirmation and shareholder ledger reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; no public filing with the Commercial Register; available to tax, FINMA, and prosecutorial authorities upon demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual board confirmation at the first meeting after the financial year-end; immediate updating upon any change in shareholding of 25% or more or change of effective control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Swiss Code of Obligations and Money Laundering Act; fine up to CHF 500,000 for serious non-compliance, criminal liability for false entries, and director disqualification; no strike-off remedy.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, and annual average of 250 full-time employees. Below these thresholds, a restricted audit (limited review) is required unless all shareholders unanimously waive the audit and the company has fewer than the statutory threshold of employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 958–960 plus Swiss GAAP FER); IFRS is mandatory for securities-listed undertakings; annually prepared in CHF.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The board of directors must maintain a current register of beneficial owners under Art. 697j CO and Art. 4 AMLA. An annual confirmation of the completeness and accuracy of the register is performed by the board before or at the AGM. No separate annual UBO filing to a Swiss central authority exists; changes are recorded without delay whenever a shareholding reaches or crosses the registration threshold.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (board and management records)
Minute Book (AGM and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–3,000 per annum for registered office and corporate agent services in Switzerland, with volume discounts in cantons such as Zug and Zurich.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000–28,000 for a mandatory ordinary audit; USD 2,000–7,000 for a restricted review; zero if a valid audit waiver is in effect.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax: 8.5% of net taxable profit after tax, equivalent to an effective federal rate of 7.83% on pre-tax profit; combined federal, cantonal and communal effective rate varies by canton — approx. 11.9% in the Canton of Zug (chosen seat) to approx. 21% in high-tax cantons.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal patent box: up to 90% of qualifying IP-derived profit exempt from cantonal and communal tax; R&D super-deduction: up to additional 50% (total deduction of 150%) of qualifying Swiss R&D labor and related costs at cantonal level; Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on excess qualifying equity available in participating cantons; participation deduction fully exempts qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial shareholdings (10% or CHF 1 million) at federal, cantonal and communal level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales), filed electronically via the Canton of Zug online portal ('TaxMe' / eTax Zug) and processed with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) through the 'Federal Tax Return' e-filing interface; VAT return filed separately via ESTV 'Swiss GST' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax authority sets a filing deadline of at least 30 days after formal request (Art. 124/125 DBG); in ordinary administrative practice for calendar-year companies in the Canton of Zug, the combined return is due by 30 June of the following year, with a routinely granted extension to 30 September; the federal direct tax assessment follows the cantonal determination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, legal form (AG), registered seat, Swiss UID / VAT number, date of incorporation, purpose and registered address of the Aktiengesellschaft.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full legal name and permanent address of every non-resident shareholder and beneficial owner must be disclosed in the ownership annex; foreign directors must be identified with passport/ID details. Nominee structures must be labelled as such.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Commercial balance sheet profit (Gewinn gemäss Handelsbilanz)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before allocation to reserves as per the audited statutory financial statements (IFRS/FC as per Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 957 ff.).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No restatement in foreign currency is required; amounts must be reported in CHF. Intercompany balances with non-resident affiliates, including shareholder loans and prepaid license revenue, must be individually itemised in the balance sheet schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of non-deductible expenses and hidden profit distributions: disproportional shareholder benefits, excessive management fees, interest paid on hidden equity, off-market intercompany royalties, and taxes at stake; also re-qualifications of economic depreciation under accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any payment to a related non-resident party that lacks arm's length support or contractual substance is re-characterised as a deemed dividend distribution, triggering 35% anticipatory tax; detailed TP documentation must accompany the relevant annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions of tax-exempt income, including the participation deduction, royalty income attributable to the IP patent box, depreciation consistent with economic use, R&D super-deduction (cantonal), and loss carryforward utilisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reductions must be evidenced with project/time-tracked documentation for R&D and per-patent income statements; for the patent box, non-resident licensors must provide proof of title in the Swiss IP register and eligible R&D cost records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable net income after add-backs and deductions; this figure is the tax base for the federal direct tax at 8.5% and the cantonal/communal income tax of Zug.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed strictly in CHF with no foreign tax credits; double taxation of the Swiss profit at both federal and cantonal level is inherent and cannot be eliminated by unilateral treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemption applied to dividends received from and capital gains on qualifying participations (at least 10% of the share capital or a participation with a market value of at least CHF 1 million) held for at least 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-owned holding structures, the deduction requires a genuine economic grouping; the tax authority may deny relief where the Swiss AG acts as a mere conduit for foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 — Patent box and R&D super-deduction (Patentbox / F&E-Abzug)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal-only relief: up to 90% of qualifying net royalties and embedded IP profits (patents, copyrighted software) are allocated to the patent box; qualifying Swiss R&D human costs may be deducted at 150%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Swiss-owned and Swiss-registered patents qualify; EdTech software must be protected by a granted patent or, in limited cases, copyright software under cantonal implementation; foreign-resident licensees' revenue share must be supported by executed license agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 — Taxable capital (Steuerbares Kapital / Capital imposable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal capital tax base: share capital, statutory and free reserves, and retained earnings, reduced by qualifying participations and self-created intangibles; Zug capital tax rate is 0.0% for taxable equity up to CHF 2 million and 0.05% thereafter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholder loans must be arm's length or re-qualified as equity (hidden equity), increasing the capital tax base and potentially triggering WHT on deemed interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late return: procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 at cantonal level and CHF 5,000 at federal level, plus default interest of 3.5% p.a. (federal rate) and cantonal surcharges; deliberate late filing after formal reminder may trigger refusal of extension and assessment by estimation with 1/3 safety margin; repeated non-filing is prosecuted as tax evasion with penalties of 25% up to 100% of the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer / impôt anticipé) applied at source on all shareholder dividend distributions of a Swiss AG (Art. 1, 13 VStG).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty reduction is granted either (a) at source, or (b) by refund. (a) Relief at source: the Swiss AG submits ESTV Form 823-825 (EUR/UK/US variants) to the Federal Tax Administration before distribution, claiming the treaty rate; approval is granted administratively under ESTV circular 1/2009 where the parent is resident in a treaty state, holds at least 10% of the votes for at least 12 months, has bona-fide economic substance, and no treaty-shopping abuse exists. (b) Refund: if the full 35% is withheld, the non-resident shareholder must file a reclaim with ESTV within 3 years of the distribution end (Art. 32 VStG), attaching: TRC (Foreign Tax Authority Form 823/824 for Switzerland), shareholding statement, audited accounts, and a beneficial owner declaration; ESTV processes refunds within 60–90 days. For Apple/Google payment rails, the AG distributes dividends subject to the same procedure; withholding obligations cannot be circumvented via foreign 'PSP' pass-through accounts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss domestic withholding tax on license and royalty outbound payments (copyrights, software IP, patents) — only potential transfer pricing taxation of the Swiss payor. Interest: 35% anticipatory tax arises only on bonds, debentures and fund-based loans documented in a Swiss securities instrument (including synthetic bearer instruments from foreign lenders); ordinary bank debt and short-term trade credit are exempt. Treaty rates: dividends 0-15% depending on the DTA and shareholding (e.g., US protocol: 0% if 10% holding; EU states commonly 5% / 15%), interest 0% under most DTAs (US 0%, UK 0%), royalties 0% under most DTAs (US 0%, UK 0%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Swiss threshold is codified; the ESTV administrative practice expects contemporaneous OECD-compliant Local File documentation where aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed CHF 500,000 (goods, services, IP, financing); the Master File is expected for groups above CHF 50 million consolidated revenue; Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for Swiss-headquartered or Swiss-included MNE groups with consolidated annual revenue of CHF 900 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland abolished the privileged holding/domicile/mixed company regimes in the 2019 Tax Reform and the Administrative Measures Act (STAF); there are no formal ESR filing regulations, but an anti-abuse economic-substance doctrine applies under Art. 21 VStG (withholding tax), Art. 6 LHID and DTA mutual agreement practice: the Swiss AG must have its administrative offices, decision-making management, qualified personnel, banking relationships and operational records in Switzerland; a passive shell relying on fiduciary office services is denied treaty benefits, WHT refunds and the patent box, and may be re-qualified as tax-transparent with profits taxed at the shareholder level.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional misrepresentation or concealment of income, falsification of subscription revenue reports (e.g., under-declared Apple/Google revenue), fabricated vendor invoices, or destruction of books (Art. 175, 186 DBG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of the entire evaded federal/cantonal tax, default interest of 3.5% p.a., penalty of 25% to 100% of the evaded tax in simple cases, and up to 200% in aggravated cases; tax fraud (use of falsified documents) carries an additional criminal fine up to CHF 30,000 and, in serious cases, publication of the decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de-facto managers face imprisonment up to 3 years for aggravated tax fraud (Art. 186 DBG); administrative fines apply to the company and responsible officers under Art. 6 VStrR; the personal assets of directors may be seized to settle the company's WHT and VAT debts where the company is insolvent (Art. 14 VStG, Art. 52 MWSTG); no travel ban is imposed for tax offences alone, but international arrest warrants and entry bans can follow repeated tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a formal registered office through a fiduciary, absence of staff, board meetings or operational decision-making in Switzerland, or routing subscription revenue through a foreign PSP and related entity to strip Swiss profit; total lack of economic substance for treaty and WHT purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the DTA-reduced dividend rate and retroactive 35% anticipatory tax plus interest; re-qualification of intercompany royalty/licence payments as deemed dividends; TP adjustment of the profit base with penalty of 25%-100%; the corporate veil is pierced for tax collection against shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for the unpaid anticipatory tax if the distribution was made and the tax not remitted; criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion; confiscation of management fees paid to the fiduciary; travel restrictions may be imposed by criminal authorities in cross-border investigation proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing of IP and financing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-charging non-resident affiliates for EdTech software licences, paying excessive royalties to a related IP company in a low-tax jurisdiction, or financing the AG through shareholder loans at non-arm's length rates; failure to maintain a valid Local File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's length adjustment to the taxable profit, recalculation of the taxable base with a penalty of 25%-100% of the tax differential; reclassification of excess shareholder loans as hidden equity with 35% anticipatory tax on deemed interest; per-diem fines for documentation default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors' criminal exposure under Art. 186 DBG for signing false statements; civil restitution claims of the tax authority against the board in insolvency proceedings; personal liability for the due-but-unpaid withholding tax on deemed dividends if the board authorised the distribution without deducting the 35% tax.
